newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador refinery shut down delays until July.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador refinery shut down delays until July.

text.p: The shutdown of Ecuador's largest oil refinery for work to modernize the plant has been delayed until mid July, an official from state-owned oil company Petroecuador said Friday.
The Esmeraldas refinery shutdown will start between July 1-15 rather than in early June as previously planned, the official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
He added the delay in the shutdown, expected for 45 to 60 days, was because two large cities are going to carry out road works which will need the supply from Esmeraldas.
Once completed at the end of 1997, the refinery's upgrade is hoped to lift production to 110,000 barrels daily from 90,000 barrels currently.
During the shutdown some 2.36 barrels of diesel and gasoline will be imported to the country, supplied by U.S. companies Coastal Petroleum and Galaxy Energy.
Ecuador, one of Latin America's largest oil producers, operates three refineries.

Esmeraldas, north-west of Quito, produced 8.11 million barrels in the first quarter, of which 3.15 million barrels of diesel and 264,000 barrels of gasoline were exported. It has a refining cost of $1.74 per barrel.
